The '''open coloring axiom''' (abbreviated '''OCA''') is an [[axiom]] about coloring edges of a [[graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] whose [[vertex (graph theory)|vertices]] are a subset of the [[real number]]s: two different versions were introduced by {{harvtxt|Abraham|Rubin|Shelah|1985}} and by {{harvtxt|Todorčević|1989}}.

==Statement==
Suppose that ''X'' is a subset of the reals, and each pair of elements of ''X'' is colored either black or white, with the set of white pairs being open in the [[complete graph]] on ''X''. The open coloring axiom states that either:
#''X'' has an [[uncountable set|uncountable]] subset such that any pair from this subset is white; or
#''X'' can be partitioned into a [[countable infinity|countable]] number of subsets such that any pair from the same subset is black.
A weaker version, '''OCA<sub>P</sub>''', replaces the uncountability condition in the first case with being a [[compact set|compact]] [[perfect set]] in ''X''. Both OCA and OCA<sub>P</sub> can be stated equivalently for arbitrary [[separable space]]s.

==Relation to other axioms==

OCA<sub>P</sub> can be proved in [[ZFC]] for [[analytic subset]]s of a [[Polish space]], and from the [[axiom of determinacy]]. The full OCA is consistent with (but independent of) ZFC, and follows from the [[proper forcing axiom]].

OCA implies that the smallest [[unbounded set]] of [[Baire space (set theory)|Baire space]] has cardinality <math>\aleph_2</math>. Moreover, assuming OCA, Baire space contains few "gaps" between sets of sequences — more specifically, that the only possible gaps are (ω<sub>1</sub>,ω<sub>1</sub>)-gaps and (κ,ω)-gaps where κ is an [[initial ordinal]] not less than ω<sub>2</sub>.
